original_test_intent: Inject a synthetic DDR5 PMIC critical-temperature shutdown condition for each applicable DIMM, prove the intended protective power action and fresh PMIC thermal evidence, then verify the device cooled logically, memory retrained and no real thermal excursion occurred.
original_method: Map DIMM/PMIC thermal sensors and I2C addresses; prove railtype7 and any valid comparator parameter; record actual PMIC/DIMM/ambient temperatures and threshold registers; inject one synthetic thermal fault under OOB/power monitoring; distinguish shutdown from reset; capture durable thermal status; enforce cooldown/clear semantics; reboot only as approved, validate memory, and restore PMIC/I2C state.
manual_activity: The thermal/PMIC owner maps each sensor and PMIC, approves a synthetic-only stimulus and exact power action, supervises one target, confirms cooldown/clear and restores memory power and bus settings.
required_inputs: Vendor proof railtype7 selects synthetic PMIC Critical Temperature Shutdown and whether voltagetype is valid/ignored
Critical threshold, hysteresis, status/latch/clear semantics and real sensor safety limits
Per-DIMM socket/die/UMC/channel/slot/dimm, PMIC address and thermal sensor mapping
Wistron BMC/platform I2C controller/bus/OOB path and expected thermal register response
Decision whether expected action is shutdown, reset or staged shutdown/reset with timing
Fresh thermal PMIC/CPER/BERT/SEL evidence, cooldown/restart/training deadlines, memory recovery and restoration
safety_requirements: Synthetic injection only; never heat hardware to trigger this review-layer case
Independent thermal, power and OOB monitoring with hard physical-temperature abort
One mapped DIMM/PMIC once; preserve status before approved clear and confirm cooldown/latched-state removal
Abort on actual temperature rise, wrong sensor/status, unexpected power action, restart loop, training failure or management loss
No automatic restart/retry/target loop; restore PMIC/I2C/telemetry/SPD/HDT settings and verify fans/sensors
agent_execution_scope: Validate synthetic stimulus, threshold/action, sensor/I2C topology, evidence, cooldown and recovery plan
Collect read-only actual temperatures, PMIC status, power/OOB timeline, CPER/BERT/SEL and post-boot memory/sensor health
Do not heat, choose targets, alter PMIC/I2C/BIOS/HDT, inject, power on/reset, repeat, recover or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve sensor matrix, synthetic stimulus and thermal limits
Supervise injection, power action and cooldown
Authorize restart, restore state and issue verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Generic PMIC/temperature log keywords cannot prove railtype7, synthetic threshold crossing, physical sensor identity or expected shutdown action.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After thermal register and power-action approval, inject one synthetic target with live physical-temperature monitoring, capture exact latched status and shutdown timeline, then clear/cool/restart only by the approved procedure.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: listvalidumc, 0:0:3, railtype7, voltagetype0/1, dimm0, immediate reset wording, all-DIMM scope, PMIC/I2C settings and 360/120-minute values remain preserved as disputed inputs.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Run a synthetic, sensor-mapped critical-temperature event one PMIC at a time with independent thermal/power evidence and controlled cooldown/restart.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds no-real-heating constraint, threshold/hysteresis, shutdown-versus-reset resolution, sensor/address mapping, cooldown and restart control.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A generic fatal reset cannot prove critical-temperature protection or safe thermal recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Confusing synthetic status with real temperature or auto-restarting before clear may cause unsafe operation or repeated shutdown.

project_override_considerations: I2C sensor/status access is BMC/platform-management scope. Require the approved controller/bus/address and retain the difference between actual measured temperature and injected status throughout evidence. Do not assume voltagetype0/1 is meaningful for railtype7.
expected_evidence: Railtype7 thermal register/threshold/hysteresis/power-action specification and per-DIMM PMIC/sensor/I2C map
Actual temperature/power/fan and raw PMIC status baseline
Exact synthetic injection with OOB shutdown/reset timeline and no real temperature excursion
Fresh critical-temperature PMIC status plus CPER/BERT/SEL source/severity
Approved latch clear/cooldown, controlled restart, full DIMM training and clean memory/sensor/fan health

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items requires Critical Temp Shutdown while Procedure says immediate reset. It also repeats voltage types0/1 for a thermal fault without defining their meaning, and requests all DIMMs from one fixed tuple. Command continuation, threshold/hysteresis, physical sensor mapping and power-action timing are absent.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The synthetic PMIC thermal-protection purpose and seed command are identifiable. Engineering can resolve the power action and thermal contract, so static review completes without real heating.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row 93 Wistron-System RAS-00813-V002: prove railtype7 is synthetic Critical Temperature Shutdown and decide whether voltagetype0/1 applies; reconcile Shutdown title with immediate Reset procedure; define threshold/hysteresis/latch/clear and no-real-heating limits; map every DIMM/PMIC thermal sensor and Wistron BMC/platform I2C controller/bus/address/OOB path; approve full tuple matrix, power-action/cooldown/restart timing, PMIC/CPER/BERT/SEL evidence, memory recovery, aborts and restoration.

review_improvement: Separates injected thermal status from real temperature and turns an ambiguous reset into a controlled shutdown/cooldown/restart validation with per-sensor attribution.
independent_technical_reasoning: A critical-temperature protection test is not another voltage-rail variant. The acceptance point is a specific PMIC thermal status crossing and its mandated power action while physical temperature stays safe. The source's voltage-type loop and reset wording may be copied from rail cases, so they require explicit engineering resolution before any action. Restart must wait for latch-clear/cooldown proof and complete memory retraining.
